source: Source: ONS, Crime in England and Wales, year ending June 2026

slides.h1: Is crime really going up in the UK?
slides.p: Two official measures for England and Wales give opposite answers. Both are right.

slides.h2: The Crime Survey: crime against people since the 1995 peak
slides.p: 19.8m incidents a year in 1995, 4.35m in the year to June 2026 (excluding fraud and computer misuse).
slides.small: Statistically significant, by the ONS’s own test

slides.h2: Police recorded crime since its 2013/14 low
slides.p: 3.51m offences then, 5.25m in the year to June 2026.
slides.small: The two measures count different things: compare trends, not levels

slides.h2: Why the police figures went up
items: In 2014 inspectors found about 1 in 5 reported crimes went unrecorded; forces tightened up
Violence, public order and sexual offences make up more than all of the 1.74m rise
Burglary recorded by police halved: victims need a crime number to claim

slides.h2: What really is rising, and what isn’t
items: Down in the survey: violence −34%, robbery −58%, burglary of homes −43%

slides.p: say crime has gone up across the country, vs in their own area (year to March 2024).
slides.small: The national picture comes from news; the local one from experience

slides.h2: How much crime is recorded where you live?
slides.p: Crimes per 1,000 residents for every police force and about 300 council areas, with the trend since 2022.
slides.small: England and Wales only. Scotland and Northern Ireland count crime differently.
